newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OECD sees higher Belgium growth, backs EMU budget.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees higher Belgium growth, backs EMU budget.

text.p: A recovery in neighbouring economies should speed up economic growth in Belgium during the next two years, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday.
Accelerated growth should put it on track to meet the criteria for the planned economic and monetary union in Europe.

The OECD, the Paris-based think-tank, said Belgian gross domestic product (GDP) should grow by 2.2 percent in 1997 after a 1.3 percent increase in 1996, helping the government cut its budget deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP from 3.2 percent.
Growth could reach 2.6 percent in 1998, while Belgium's debt should fall to 124.5 percent of GDP from 130.0 percent in 1996.
After picking up in 1996 due to indirect tax increases, inflation should be more moderate in 1997.
Unemployment was, however, likely to remain high, the OECD said, noting recent declines in the jobless rate were due partly to the removal of older workers from the official figures.
The OECD said the 1997 budget, with its package of savings and tax increases amounting to 80 billion Belgian francs, was unlikely to have a negative impact on households' real spending.
"Given their sizeable net financial position, households can largely preserve their spending pattern by further reducing the saving ratio," the OECD said.
